newsitem.title: USA: Mississippi corn harvest progresses, cotton starts.
newsitem.headline: Mississippi corn harvest progresses, cotton starts.

text.p: Mississippi corn and soybean harvest progressed steadily and the cotton harvest began in the week ended Sunday, the state's Agricultural Statistics Service said.

Boll rot in cotton became a major concern in parts of the state that have had excess rainfall, it said. Cotton was rated 64 percent good to ecellent, down four points from last week. Soil moisture was rated 71 percent adequate, 11 pct surplus.
Cotton opening bolls 84 pct vs 77 week ago, 78 year ago, 59 on a five-year average.
Cotton harvested 2 pct vs nil w/a, 2 yr ago, 1 avg.
Afternoon rains slowed corn harvesting but benefited fall and winter grasses, the report said.
Corn was 53 percent harvested versus 38 pct last week, 61 pct last year and 41 avg. Corn was 97 pct mature.
Soybeans harvested 17 pct vs 9 w/a, 10 y/a, 2 avg.
Sorghum harvested 62 pct vs 53 w/a, 49 y/a, 42 avg.
Rice harvested 25 pct vs 18 w/a, 53 y/a, 25 avg.
